title: Research on Poverty
subtitle: Papers Co-authored with Low or Lower-Middle Income Countries

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) actively promotes international research collaborations to enhance the quality, visibility, and global relevance of its research. During the reporting period, the University published 23 research papers related to SDG 1 – No Poverty. Of these, 21 publications (91.30%) were authored by researchers based in India, while 2 publications (8.70%) were developed through international collaborations.
The University's international research collaborations include:

items: 1 publication (4.30%) co-authored with researchers from Bahrain and Malaysia.
1 publication (4.30%) co-authored with researchers from the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

contentBlocks.text: These collaborations demonstrate the University's commitment to fostering international academic partnerships and promoting the exchange of knowledge on issues related to poverty alleviation, financial inclusion, sustainable development, and inclusive economic growth.

At present, no publications were co-authored with institutions from low or lower-middle income countries during the assessment period. Consequently, the University records 0 publications (0.00%) under this specific THE Impact Rankings metric.

The University is actively working to expand its global research network and encourages faculty members to establish collaborative partnerships with institutions in low and lower-middle income countries through joint research projects, academic exchange programmes, international conferences, and funded research initiatives. These efforts are expected to strengthen future research collaborations that contribute directly to the achievement of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 1 – No Poverty.

title: No Poverty: Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI)
subtitle: Citation Performance and Scholarly Influence on Poverty Eradication

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) is committed to producing high-quality, impactful research that contributes to the achievement of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1 – No Poverty. The University's research addresses critical themes such as poverty alleviation, financial inclusion, rural development, agricultural finance, employment generation, economic resilience, and inclusive growth.

During the reporting period, the University published 23 research publications aligned with SDG 1. Of these, 21 publications (91.30%) were authored by researchers based in India, while 2 publications (8.70%) were developed through international collaborations with researchers from Bahrain, Malaysia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These collaborations have enhanced the global visibility and academic reach of the University's research.

The Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) is used to assess the citation performance of research outputs by comparing the number of citations received with the global average for publications of the same subject area, document type, and publication year. Through publications in reputed Scopus-indexed journals, IEEE conference proceedings, and Springer publications, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) strives to produce research that is internationally relevant and contributes to evidence-based policymaking and sustainable development.

The University's SDG 1 research reflects its emphasis on scholarly excellence, interdisciplinary collaboration, and generating knowledge that supports poverty reduction, financial inclusion, and inclusive socio-economic development. The institution continues to encourage high-impact research, international collaborations, and publications in globally recognized journals to further enhance its research influence and citation performance.
